s1.syndrome_frame: Abdominal pain and mass with acute exacerbation
salient_findings: Palpable, movable mass in the upper abdomen
Large echogenic mass in the gastric antrum on ultrasound
Large submucosal bulging mass in the posterior gastric wall on endoscopy
key_facts: 63-year-old woman
Insidious upper abdominal pain unrelated to food ingestion
Nausea
Episode of intense acute abdominal pain
No hematemesis or melena
Untreated dyslipidemia
Well-controlled hypertension on methyldopa
Smoker of ten cigarettes per day
No family history of cancer
Normal physical examination except for abdominal mass
Normal laboratory tests, including complete blood count
No anemia
Abdominal ultrasound showed large echogenic mass in gastric antrum
Endoscopy revealed large submucosal bulging mass in posterior gastric wall
Biopsy attempts failed to sample submucosal mass
Ulcer biopsies showed only necrotic mucosa
Contrast-enhanced CT showed well-defined, homogeneous, oval mass arising from posterior gastric wall
